# A method of a generic struct that writes it, `Tally[V].keep`, called in a
# generic component on the two-way prop that names the program's tally. The
# call names the component's V until the splice binds it, so passMonomorphize
# kept the method, and the copying after the splice left the program's own
# generics alone: fyne and bubbletea called `TallyKeep(m.tally, …)`, taking
# the uncopied `Tally` the spliced call no longer had.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

// Counts kept by key.
struct Tally[V any] {
    counts map[string, V]
}

// Keeps `v` under `key`.
func Tally[V].keep(this ref[Tally[V]], key string, v V) {
    this.counts[key] = v
}

var tally = Tally[int]{counts={}}

// Writes the tally it is handed through a method of the tally's own, at the
// component's parameter.
component keeper[V any](key string, value V, :into Tally[V]) ui.node {
    ui.button #keep(text=key, @click { into.keep(key, value) })
}

component page ui.node {
    keeper #keeper(key="a", value=1, :into=tally)
}

func testAMethodOfAGenericStructWritesThroughTheProp(t test.Test, c page) {
    c.keeper.keep.click()
    t.assert(tally.counts["a"] == 1)
}

ui.window {
    page()
}
